title: Canh Chua: Vietnamese Sour Catfish Soup with Tamarind and Pineapple
summary: A southern Vietnamese sour soup: catfish steaks poached in a tamarind broth with pineapple, tomato, okra and taro stems, finished with crunchy bean sprouts, fresh herbs and golden fried garlic.

ingredients.item: skin-on catfish steaks, about 2.5 cm thick
ingredients.note: or any firm freshwater fish steaks

ingredients.item: ripe tomatoes, each cut into 8 wedges
okra pods, sliced on the diagonal
bạc hà (taro stems), peeled and sliced on the diagonal
ingredients.note: leave out if you cannot find it; add 4 more okra

ingredients.item: Thai basil and rice-paddy herb (ngò om) leaves

steps.title: Season the fish
steps.text: Pat the catfish steaks dry, toss them with the 2 tsp fish sauce and the pepper and leave while you prepare everything else.

steps.title: Soak the tamarind
steps.text: Pour the 250 ml hot water over the tamarind pulp, leave 10 min, then squeeze and mash it with your fingers. Push it through the sieve into a bowl and throw away the fibres and seeds.

steps.title: Fry the garlic
steps.text: Warm the oil in the small pan over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and stir for 2-3 min until pale gold. Tip the garlic and its oil into a bowl straight away; it keeps darkening off the heat.

steps.title: Make the broth
steps.text: Bring the 1.2 litres water to the boil in the saucepan. Stir in the strained tamarind liquid, sugar and the 1.5 tbsp fish sauce, then lower to a steady simmer.

steps.title: Poach the fish
steps.text: Slide in the catfish steaks and simmer gently, skimming any foam, for 8-10 min until the flesh flakes and reaches 63 °C at the thickest part. Lift them into serving bowls with the slotted spoon.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the pineapple and okra to the pot and simmer 3 min. Add the tomatoes and taro stems and cook 1-2 min more, just until the tomatoes soften at the edges and the stems turn glossy.

steps.title: Balance
steps.text: Taste the broth: it should be sour first, then sweet and salty. Add a little more sugar or a squeeze of lime to adjust, but no more fish sauce.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Put a handful of bean sprouts in each bowl, ladle the hot broth and vegetables over the fish, then top with the herbs, a spoon of the fried garlic and its oil, and chilli if you like. Serve with rice and lime wedges.

tips: Taste the broth before the fish goes in: sour should lead, with sweet and salty behind it.
Fry the garlic slowly and pull it off the heat when pale gold; it turns bitter if it browns.
Add the tomatoes and taro stems at the very end so they keep their shape and crunch.
Find bạc hà and ngò om in Vietnamese grocers; Thai basil stands in for ngò om, and extra okra for bạc hà.
storage: Best eaten straight away. Leftover broth (without the sprouts and herbs) keeps 1 day in the fridge; bring it to the boil before serving. Not suitable for freezing. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
